newsitem.title: USA: Metal Management closing on Cozzi merger.
newsitem.headline: Metal Management closing on Cozzi merger.

text.p: Metal Management Inc said Thursday it closed on a previously announced merger agreement with Cozzi Iron & Metal Inc.
It said Cozzi holders are likely to receive 11.5 million shares of the company's common stock and $6 million in cash.

At the effective time of the merger, Metal Management said it intends to name Albert Cozzi as president and chief operating officer of the merged company. T. Benjamin Jennings will remain chairman of the board and chief development officer, and Gerard Jacobs will remain the chief executive officer of the merged entity.
Frank Cozzi will be a vice president of the company and president of the Cozzi operations.

If the Cozzi merger is completed as contemplated, Albert Cozzi, Frank Cozzi, Greg Cozzi, T. Benjamin Jennings and Gerard Jacobs will own, directly or indirectly, about 15.7 million of the company's common stock on a fully diluted basis.
Giving the effect to the Cozzi merger, as of March 31, 1997, the company had about 27.3 million shares of common stock on a fully diluted basis.

As previously reported, Metal Management, Proler Southwest Inc, and Proler Steelworks LLC have signed a binding leter of intent to merge the three companies with Metal Management as the surviving entity.

Metal Management said at the closing, the transaction would be accomplished by the company acquiring all of the equity interests in Proler Southwest and Proler Steelworks for $15 million in cash, a $2 million promissory note, 1.75 million shares of common stock in the company and 375,000 warrants exercisable for five years at $6 per share.
Parties in both the Cozzi and Proler transactions are proceeding with their due dilligence investigations. Both meregers are expected to be completed by summer, Metal Management said.

Metal Management also disclosed terms of a previously proposed purchase of Reserve Iron Metal LP through the purchase of all of the common stock of P. Joseph Iron & Metal Inc, sole general partner of Reserve, and all of the limited partnership units in Reserve. It will pay $5.9 million and a promissiory note for about $1.5 million.

In addition, Metal Management said it agreed in principle to amend the purchase agreement for Reserve. It said certain sellers of Reserve agreed to indemnify the company and its affiliates against a significant portion of specified potential liabilities.
